title: Demonstrative adjectives (ce, cet, cette, ces)
summary: ce + masculine singular noun: ce village, ce garçon.
cet + masculine singular noun starting with a vowel or silent h: cet hôtel, cet ami, cet été.
cette + feminine singular noun, even before a vowel: cette ville, cette école.
ces + any plural noun, masculine or feminine: ces magasins, ces filles, ces hôtels.
They mean 'this' or 'that' (ces = 'these' or 'those'); the context tells you which.
Choose ce or cet by the very next word: ce nouvel hôtel (n is a consonant), cet énorme gâteau (é is a vowel).
Add -ci (here) or -là (there) to the noun to contrast two things: ce pull-ci (this jumper) / ce pull-là (that jumper).
Useful time phrases: ce matin, ce soir, ce week-end, cet été, cet hiver, cette semaine, cette année.

cards.front: What are the four forms of the demonstrative adjective (this / that / these / those)?
cards.back: ce (m sg): ce livre; cet (m sg before a vowel or silent h): cet arbre, cet hôtel; cette (f sg): cette rue; ces (all plurals): ces livres, ces rues.

cards.en: Have you already seen this film?
cards.why: film is masculine singular and starts with a consonant: ce.
chaussures is plural: ces is used for all plurals, masculine or feminine.

cards.front: When do you use cet rather than ce?
cards.back: Before a masculine singular word starting with a vowel or silent h, so the sounds run together: cet ordinateur, cet homme, cet été, cet hiver. Feminine nouns always take cette, even before a vowel: cette école, cette amie.

cards.prompt: ___ hôtel est trop cher pour nous.
cards.en: This hotel is too expensive for us.
cards.why: hôtel is masculine singular and starts with a silent h: cet.

cards.prompt: Nous allons faire du ski ___ hiver.
cards.why: hiver is masculine and starts with a silent h: cet hiver (like cet été).

cards.en: This year I'm taking my exams.
cards.why: année is feminine, so cette – never cet, even though it starts with a vowel.

cards.front: Ce or cet? ___ nouvel appartement / ___ énorme gâteau
cards.back: Look at the very next word, not the noun: ce nouvel appartement (nouvel starts with a consonant), cet énorme gâteau (énorme starts with a vowel).

cards.why: gâteau is masculine and the next word, énorme, starts with a vowel: cet.
The next word, nouvel, starts with a consonant, so ce – even though appartement starts with a vowel.

cards.front: How do you contrast 'this one (here)' with 'that one (there)'?
cards.back: Add -ci or -là to the noun with a hyphen: Je prends ce pull-ci, pas ce pull-là (this jumper, not that one). Cette robe-ci est plus chère que cette robe-là.

cards.prompt: Quel pull préfères-tu : ce pull-ci ou ce pull-___ ?
cards.en: Which jumper do you prefer: this one or that one?
cards.why: -là (with a grave accent) points to the one further away; -ci to the nearer one.

cards.front: How do you say this morning, this evening, this week, this summer and this year?
cards.back: ce matin, ce soir, cette semaine, cet été, cette année. Also: ce week-end, cet hiver, cet après-midi.

cards.why: école is feminine, so cette. L' hides the gender – the adjective grande shows it.
